title: September Jobs Report Shows Just 29,000 New Jobs as AI Cuts Mount
key_facts: U.S. nonfarm payrolls rose by 29,000 in September 2026, in the Bureau of Labor Statistics report released Friday 2 Oct; economists polled by Dow Jones had expected about 84,000 (article cites CNBC).
The unemployment rate rose to 4.2%; the forecast was that it would hold at 4.1%.
Revisions removed another 60,000 jobs from earlier months.
Average hourly earnings rose 0.1% on the month (0.3% forecast) and 3% over the year (3.2% expected).

BMW said on 30 Sep it plans to cut about 20% of its senior management, roughly 100 of 465 top positions, using AI to flatten its hierarchy, with cuts landing by mid-2027 as part of a plan to shed 8,000 jobs (article cites Bloomberg).
The article says AI is the most cited reason employers give for layoffs this year, with about 150,000 announced cuts attributed to it since 2023, almost two-thirds of them in the first half of 2026.
Stock futures rose and Treasury yields fell after the report; traders bet the Federal Reserve is less likely to raise rates at its 27-28 October meeting (article cites CNBC).

Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari said on 30 Sep that AI-related investment accounts for roughly half of the economy's 2% growth over the past year, but he doubts the rest of the economy is contracting.
quote_evidence: The U.S. economy added only 29,000 jobs in September, far below the roughly 84,000 Wall Street expected, while the unemployment rate climbed to 4.2%.
Revisions wiped another 60,000 jobs off prior months.
AI has become the single most cited reason employers give for layoffs this year.
why_it_matters_hint: A very weak jobs report arrives while companies openly name AI as a reason for cuts, but the article links the two without showing that AI caused the weak numbers.
event_date: Friday 2 Oct 2026 (BLS jobs report for September 2026)
notes: Secondary outlet citing CNBC and Bloomberg; the BLS figures were not checked at the source. Commentary about markets and 'risk assets' in the article was not used. BMW cuts and Kashkari remarks are background dated 30 Sep 2026.
